The approach, leg by leg:

The existing `bootOnce(tag, env, prepare)` is reused with `STUB_REPORT`/`STUB_GATE_RECEIPT` overridden in `env` — its spread puts the case's env after the file's own three-item fixture.
- FIVE new boots, all started eagerly beside the file's existing four: `fourteen` (a `STUB_TYPESAFE_ANSWERS` file mapping needle `pNN` to the score the Context pins), `onlyP05` (p05 at 2.5, every other piece 1.0), `exit7` (`STUB_TYPESAFE_EXIT=7` over the same fixture), `allLow` (every piece 2.4), and `rigDefault` (the rig's own report and receipt, the default reply at 0.8).
- (a) [M1] the fourteen boot's body: the line after the table's last `| … |` row is blank, the next is exactly `Act on these: 11 of 14`, then blank, then exactly ten consecutive `- ` lines string-equal to the entries for p04 p01 p07 p14 p06 p13 p05 p12 p02 p10 at 3.0 2.9 2.8 2.8 2.7 2.7 2.6 2.6 2.5 2.5, then blank, then `Residuals: 14 from review`; p11/p03/p08/p09's texts absent from every line above that; and `onlyP05` renders `Act on these: 1 of 14` with p05's single entry at `attention 2.5`.
- (b) [M2] `rigDefault`, `exit7` and `allLow` each carry no line beginning `Act on these`.
- (c) [M3] the fourteen boot's body with its `Act on these`-to-`Residuals:` span spliced out is string-equal to `exit7`'s; both carry `Residuals: 14 from review`, `Amendments: none` and fourteen `- [ ] task 1 reviewer — ` lines under `### Residuals` in checklist order; same `mergePuts` length; the fourteen boot's `typesafe.log` holds exactly fourteen lines.

The one sub-clause the exam cannot encode is leg (c)'s last: "the first `Run:` runs the card-cells sim green on the edited script". `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` M4 forbids a sim from spawning another sim, so that reading stays the driver's `Run:` line, named in the file header and returned under `unsatisfiable`. payload.body:
Approach for task 1 (the card's `Act on these` section).

Site: `card_head` (fleet/sandbox-boot.sh ~2787) is one single-quoted `python3 -c` program. The section goes between the task table loop and the `Residuals:` line built at ~3003, appended as `["", "Act on these: <q> of <n>", ""] + entries` so the existing `out += ["", "Residuals: ..."]` supplies the trailing blank — which makes M3's splice (from the `Act on these` line up to, not including, the `Residuals:` line) yield exactly the no-section body.

Rows: `render_card` already reads `residuals="$(residual_items || true)"`; it will also read `rows="$(residual_rows || true)"` and pass it to `card_head` as a THIRD ARGV STRING (the Context allows argument, file or second stdin document). No new file, no new request — `rows` mode never calls `fleet_curl`, it reads the cache `residual_jev` filled inside `collect_evidence`.

Zip by index: `checklist` and `rows` modes are two calls of the same `residual_read` walk over the same two documents, so the nth row is the nth checklist item. The entry takes its `<name> — <text>` off the checklist item verbatim and its attention/actor/status/subject off the row's `jev`; a row whose request failed has no `jev` key and is not a candidate.

Threshold 2.5 inclusive, `"%.1f"`, sort by -attention (stable, so ties keep checklist order), cap at ten, and no section at all when no row qualifies. Nothing gates on it.

Done and committed as `8fda0be5`, footprint exactly the task's Files: `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` and `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_residuals.mjs`.

What landed: `render_card` reads `rows="$(residual_rows || true)"` beside the checklist it already read and passes it to `card_head` as $3, which rides argv as the python program's seventh argument. `act_now(items)` zips the rows onto the stdin checklist BY INDEX — the two renderings are two calls of the same `residual_read` walk over the same receipt and report, so the nth row scores the nth item — and appends `["", "Act on these: <q> of <n>", ""] + entries` right after the table loop. The existing `out += ["", "Residuals: ..."]` supplies the trailing blank, which is what makes M3's splice exact.

Threshold `2.5` inclusive, `"%.1f"`, `picks.sort(key=lambda pick: -pick[0])` (stable, so ties keep checklist order), `picks[:10]`, and an empty `picks` returns `[]` — no header, no blank line.

Note for a later session: `card_head`'s program is `python3 -c '…'` in single quotes, so nothing added there may hold an apostrophe — that ruled out the obvious comment wordings and is why the new comments read the way they do.

Green: `test_sandbox_boot_residuals.mjs` (18/18, including the four new legs over a fourteen-piece fixture), `test_sandbox_boot_card_cells.mjs`, `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_amendments.mjs` (the pin the Context names), and `fleet/roles/` is untouched.

payload.body:
examiner: the exam is written and red at BASE for one reason — the section does not exist.

`node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_residuals.mjs` at BASE: run-178's fourteen legs all still green, three of this task's cases red:

- `(a) [M1] the section stands between the table and the \`Residuals:\` line, ten entries deep` — "the line after that is exactly \`Act on these: 11 of 14\`"
- `(a) [M1] one qualifying row renders a one-entry section` — "renders \`Act on these: 1 of 14\`"
- `(c) [M3] splicing the section out yields the failed run's body, byte for byte` — "the section must stand above the \`Residuals:\` line, or there is nothing to splice out"

TWO READINGS a later session would otherwise reconstruct.

1. WHERE THE BLANK LINES FALL, which is what the implementer has to get right and what leg (a) pins positionally. BASE's `card_head` closes the table with `out += ["", "Residuals: %d from review" % len(items)]`. M1 asks for `tableRow, "", "Act on these: q of n", "", entries…, "", "Residuals:"` — so the section the implementer appends after the table's rows is `["", "Act on these: …", "", *entries]` and BASE's own `["", "Residuals:"]` supplies the trailing blank. Any other split renders a doubled blank, and leg (c)'s splice — from the `Act on these` line up to, not including, the `Residuals:` line — then stops being BASE's body. I checked the arithmetic both ways before pinning the indices: the split above splices back to BASE exactly.

2. `tableEnd` IS SCOPED ABOVE THE COUNT LINE. The record below the fold opens with a table of its own, so the body's LAST `| … |` line is `| vm | … |`, not the task row. The helper searches only the lines above the `Residuals:` count line and then asserts the row it found starts `| 1 | ` — otherwise leg (a) would be reading the seam between the record's vm row and `### Checks` and would pass on a card with no section at all.

THE FIXTURE, for the implementer: the rig's `DEFAULT_REPORT` with a fourteen-piece `notes` (`p01 …` through `p14 …`, joined by `; `) and the rig's default `{"verdict":"PASS"}` receipt — fourteen `task 1 reviewer` items, no ack, no `actor`, no amendment, so the card below the section is `Residuals: 14 from review`, no errand line, `Amendments: none`. Verified at BASE: fourteen requests, fourteen rows, one merge PUT, the scores landing as the Context pins them (p09 at 2.49, p02/p10/p11 at exactly 2.5). Five boots, each started eagerly beside run-178's four; the whole file runs in about 4s.

UNSATISFIABLE, one sub-clause. Leg (c) closes on "the first `Run:` runs the card-cells sim green on the edited script". `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` M4 forbids a sim from spawning — or even naming for an `existsSync` — another sim, so that reading cannot be made inside this file. It stays the driver's `Run:` line, and the file header says so. The reading this exam can make of the same seam is leg (c)'s splice, which pins every line of the body outside the section, the task table's last row included.
